## 2026-11-02 — MQTT physical retirement notifications

Adopted the separately committed, prototype-proven Core `net_tcp_retire` module
in `xmqtt_client`. Client Wait/Destroy no longer use fixed Sleep(1) observations
or an ownership graph Count operation as a concurrent operational wait. The
Client owns an embedded mutex/condition dedicated to actual reference retirement.
A load/CAS drop above two returns without subsequent Client access; terminal
2->1 publication and notification share the wait lock. The admission Gate is
never acquired under that lock, since post rollback can drop a reference while
Gate is held. All primitives initialize/unwind/free with the Client, including
factory failures. Existing producer/post/timer/request/native/event owners remain
real obligations. After the caller-only Client state, the same remaining timeout
budget feeds `xrtNetStreamWaitRetired` for the native callback tail. The native
phase rounds that remaining budget to public milliseconds, rather than starting
a fresh full timeout. Timeout preserves the caller owner.

Multiple waiters borrow one stable caller owner; all borrowers and API entries
must finish before Destroy. Engine workers remain rejected, including a CLOSED
notification. Repeated Close on CLOSED returns without posting a new task.
Application Close stays abortive; this change adds no normal MQTT DISCONNECT,
protocol feature, worker, shared runtime, busy-spin or timer-resolution change.

## 2026-11-02 — explicit zero-timeout MQTT retirement polls

Final review after `1bb84eb` found that the zero-timeout path relied on a later
monotonic clock read advancing beyond nextafter(now). Make zero explicit in both
Client-reference and native phases, so an unchanged timer tick cannot turn a
poll into a one-millisecond condition/native wait. Positive and infinite waits
keep the previous remaining-budget behavior. The caller owner, public layouts,
protocol handling and module closure are unchanged.

suite in modular and single forms (four program executions), including zero
polls on open/retired Clients, finite waits on held CLOSED callbacks, multiple
borrowers, 32 wake races, OOM and original-error cases. The generated single
implementation matches. This follow-up is verified locally; the complete package
and performance evidence above belongs specifically to `1bb84eb`, rather than a
new measurement claim for this two-guard correction. Its source snapshot and
original artifacts are retained, and all new commands/hashes are under
`out/service-extensions/xmqtt-retirement-zero/`. No performance rerun was selected
and neither noise failure nor pending full/native qualification is waived.

## 2026-11-02 — bounded application MQTT DISCONNECT

Implemented `xmqttClientDisconnectAsync` and its off-worker blocking counterpart
for MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1. After accepted CONNACK, admission atomically stops new
requests only after its encoded snapshot, quota result, Future/producer token
and worker wake are committed. A NULL packet means normal reason zero. One
operation reserves one existing request slot and its wire/object budgets; quota,
validation, peer-cap/expiry and OOM failure leave the caller output unchanged and
do not turn an open connection into a closing one. Duplicate/closed admission
and ordinary overload preserve ambient error. The request metadata and typed
write result are reused; there is no new runtime, thread, operation dispatch or
public structure layout change.

The sole protocol owner keeps draining prior accepted PUBLISH outcomes, partial
PUBLISH/PING/receiver-PUBACK frames and QoS1 acknowledgements before sending the
final DISCONNECT. Each earlier request retains its own typed outcome/deadline;
unsent expiry/restriction need not make a healthy connection fail. The shutdown
has one finite API-entry deadline through encoding, all drain work and native
queue close. Zero is explicitly expired, independently of timer precision.
Explicit Future cancellation wakes the owner; raw token requests are sampled on
progress/deadline. Cancellation, abortive Close or the first connection/resource
failure interrupts the operation without reopening admission or appending an
additional packet after a partial frame. Once final output starts, keep-alive
processing stops. Existing timer/send nodes and actual producer/native leases
remain real obligations through physical retirement.

A successful result means normal native drain/close, not a broker acknowledgement,
Will guarantee or proof that every preceding PUBLISH succeeded. The Future keeps
AcceptedBytes, requested Reason, first Status/Cause, Identifier=0 and Puback=NULL;
any accepted prefix remains MAY_HAVE_REACHED_PEER even on OK. Retained results
outlive Client and Engine. Wait additionally observes all actual reference tails.
The final Status snapshot and CLOSED publication share the admission gate, so a
racing explicit Close cannot produce mismatched Future and Info outcomes.
Application callbacks can request asynchronous shutdown; blocking helpers reject
all workers of the same Engine.

The independent protocol basis is OASIS MQTT 5.0 sections 3.14/3.14.2.2.2 and
MQTT 3.1.1 section 3.14, linked in the client documentation. The wire peer checks
normal/0x04 final bytes, reason/user-property snapshot lifetime, original CONNECT
expiry constraints, exact peer packet caps, ordering and client-initiated EOF.
The 0x04 fixture verifies the requested wire reason, not actual broker Will
publication. Pinned broker Will/session interoperability remains required.

### Final verification

Windows O2 and WSL O2 ASan/UBSan pass seven modular plus seven selected single
programs each. Added normal/byte-at-a-time shutdown, held QoS1 ACK drain,
per-request drain timeout, cancellation, explicit abort, first protocol error,
pre-CONNACK and quota rejection, allocation-budget rollback/success/lifetimes,
retained outcome and 32 explicit-Close completion races. The race requires the
Future Status and final Info CloseStatus to agree, allowing either legal winner.

Independent stdlib socket peers pass 1070 cases: the existing (31 basic + 37
sender QoS1 + 30 receiver QoS1 + 23 diagnostics) in modular/static/shared on both
platforms, plus 43 application-shutdown cases in modular/single/static/shared on
both. New cases include zero expiry, fragmented receiver ACK, partial prior
PUBLISH, immutable properties, peer size/expiry constraints, held-ACK drain,
quota/admission, duplicate shutdown, partial final-frame abort/timeout, immediate
and posted reentrant Close, slow reader and final EOF with no further packets.
A before-CONNACK local abort may legitimately cancel TCP before peer accept;
the fixture permits only that absent-connection case, not an accepted socket leak.

The initial receive-ACK fixture incorrectly classified every `_ack` name as an
outgoing QoS1 test and added an unintended PUBLISH. Both platform failures and
the previous driver are retained under `before-case-classification-fix/`;
explicit case classification fixes the fixture without dropping the ACK case.
A successful earlier candidate is preserved under `before-explicit-zero/`.
Zero-deadline and final-status publication were then tightened, followed by the
final complete matrix; no stale earlier artifacts support this final stage.

Minimal/full static/shared package consumers pass on both platforms (eight).
The original healthy echo/error examples and the new offline graceful example
run on both (six executions). The new example checks QoS1 PUBACK, final normal
DISCONNECT, peer EOF, physical Stream/Client/Listener/Engine cleanup and a retained
result. Both new entry points compile through declaration-only single headers.
Trim/feature/amalgamation/reference/layout/prefix checks pass, and the existing
build/package/API-reference/performance-tool subset reports 78 tests, OK. The
prior Core TCP assertion/size-gate and global xhttp failures remain unresolved;
no fully green global suite is claimed. WSL is development evidence, not native

## MQTT current-connection QoS-2 sender (2026-11-02)

Baseline: `6d3ae7aca68a0279e1abed60197805f66b0ae3c5`. The developing client
now admits fresh QoS-2 PUBLISH on MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1, using the existing bounded
QoS-1/2 identifier table and native-owned request lifetime. Positive PUBREC
schedules immutable inline PUBREL; successful final completion waits for
PUBCOMP. Send credit remains held through PUBCOMP or negative PUBREC. Negative
PUBCOMP (including id-not-found) describes the protocol result, not proof of
non-delivery. There is no PUBLISH replay, timer retransmission, reconnect or
session store in this slice. Unknown/early PUBCOMP cannot complete a different
flow or mint credit; unknown PUBREC/wrong-kind/unsent ACKs close with PROTOCOL.

Repeated successful PUBREC coalesces while release is unsent/partial and repeats
the immutable frame after a complete release. A terminal ACK arriving during a
partial repeat defers logical completion until that frame boundary. Native
release tails retain the actual request and its identifier; no borrowed stack
buffer is passed to TCP. Timeout/cancellation/Close after an accepted prefix
retires the connection with uncertain delivery. Graceful shutdown drains the
final ACK and partial release before its final packet. No Core or new shared
runtime changes were needed.

The typed result appends independent owned Pubrec/Pubcomp messages and scalar
receipt/completion flags. Scalar reasons/decisions are recorded before metadata
allocation; quota failure may therefore return LIMIT with the protocol decision
still available. ACK properties survive Client/Engine destruction and can be
retained independently. Duplicate positive receipts make no additional ACK
copy. Original PUBLISH wire stays charged through actual request retirement,
even after PUBREC. AcceptedBytes excludes release bytes.

Measured layout on both tested x64 ABIs: write result 40 -> 64 bytes, preserving
the complete old prefix (Puback offset 32; Pubrec starts at 40); request 96 ->
104 bytes. Those requested-size costs also affect QoS-0/1 and shutdown. Private
Client remains 1144 Windows / 1352 WSL bytes; public config/info/ready/packet/
codec/property remain 272/160/136/168/56/40. Struct sizes do not measure allocator
buckets, RSS, all copies or throughput/P99. PUBREC and PUBCOMP each consume an
owned message in the existing object budget. No zero-cost claim is made.

modular/single programs. All 7 modular + 7 single programs per OS pass, together
with minimal/full static/shared package consumers, four offline client examples
per OS, declaration-only/prefix layout, trimming, generated features/single/API
checks and 78 build/package/API-reference/performance-tool regression tests.
The new QoS-2 stdlib socket peer has 37 cases on each of modular/single/static/
shared, each on both OSes (296 new cases). Existing basic/QoS1/receive/error
cases remain 121 x 6; graceful cases remain 43 x 8: 1366 total independent wire
cases, 28 modular/single programs, 8 package consumers and 8 example executions.

## MQTT volatile QoS-2 receiver (2026-11-02)

Baseline: `3e749c88c83aba39043b6f76ca660ec0fe0f9544`. The developing client
now accepts incoming MQTT 5.0/3.1.1 QoS-2 exchanges: one owned message enters
the bounded application queue before PUBREC; the incoming id remains active
through complete PUBCOMP acceptance into ordered native output. Application
Take/Release does not return protocol credit. QoS-1 pending PUBACKs and active
QoS-2 ids share CONNECT Receive Maximum; incoming/outgoing ids are independent.

Active duplicate PUBLISH repeats/coalesces PUBREC without another local enqueue,
message copy or Received increment, regardless of DUP. PUBREL completes the
sequence without another delivery, including an early release queued behind its
PUBREC. Unknown/repeated PUBREL receives minimal PUBCOMP (unknown reason 0x92 in
v5); it creates no application message or credit. After PUBCOMP, PUBLISH may
reuse the id even with DUP=1. Forbidden properties, cross-QoS active-id reuse,
peer packet caps and receive-window violations retain typed failure semantics.
This is volatile local enqueue on the current connection, not crash-safe or
business exactly-once delivery. Session/persistence/reconnect remain required.

A private direct-index state table is lazy on the first QoS-2 PUBLISH or unknown
PUBREL. Its fixed x64 header/state size is 65576 bytes, plus four bytes for each
of 2*min(MaxMessages,ReceiveMaximum) ACK slots: 66088 requested bytes at default
settings, 65584 with Receive Maximum=1. It is charged to MaxPrivateBytes and
cached through Destroy. It stores no message reference and has at most 65535
active ids. Application queue/retained-object count and byte limits remain
independent. Private Client adds one pointer: Windows 1144 -> 1152; WSL 1352 ->
1360. Request remains 104; public config/info/ready/write/packet/codec/property
remain 272/160/136/64/168/56/40. Struct sizes do not establish allocator/RSS or
throughput/tail cost.

The finite control queue coalesces queued duplicates and uses native copied
output; native buffers may still allocate. Complete ACK frames alternate
between ready QoS-1 and QoS-2 classes, preventing a replenished QoS-1 ring from
monopolizing small write budgets. Partial frames keep priority, with byte/chunk/
packet work bounds. New QoS-2 ids also scan the bounded pending QoS-1 ring to
reject cross-QoS collisions. There is no claim of zero overhead for inactive
paths, duplicate traffic, cold allocation or control scheduling. Graceful
shutdown drains accepted incoming flows and ACKs within its original finite
deadline; timeout/cancel/Close aborts without fabricating completion. Queued
messages remain available independently of transport failure.

Two negative controls are retained. The pre-fix receiver fails the deterministic
ACK-fairness socket case (a buffered QoS-1 backlog delays PUBREC). Separately, a
test-only readiness barrier proves that accepted submissions arriving after a
worker's initial collection could be stranded if graceful Close failed in that
same turn. The failure path now recollects accepted submissions before settling
the disconnect request. The gated test verifies both typed Futures and balanced
physical accounting. Logs are `windows-before-ack-fairness.json/.log` and
`windows-before-queued-close-fix.log`; the previously observed WSL single graceful
abort failure is retained in `before-final-boundaries-wsl-single-graceful-wire.log`.
An existing diagnostic fixture now waits for the peer callback before asserting
its final reason; local physical close alone cannot prove that observation. A
local verification-helper output-path typo was also corrected, without changing
library behavior. All final runs below use the corrected inputs.

Verification: native Windows GCC O2 and WSL GCC O2, with ASan/UBSan/leak halt for
modular and single programs. All 7 modular + 7 single programs per OS, minimal/
full static/shared consumers, five offline client examples per OS, declaration-
only/prefix layouts, trim and generated feature/single/reference checks pass.
The separate stdlib receiver peer now has 66 cases on modular/single/static/
shared for each OS (528 new cases). Existing basic/QoS1/receive/error cases
remain 121 x 6; graceful cases 43 x 8; sender cases 37 x 8: 1894 total independent
wire cases, 28 modular/single programs, 8 package consumers, 10 example executions.
The old receive peer's two unsupported-QoS2 expectations now verify the real
handshake and peer-observed barrier. The 78 build/package/API-reference/
performance-tool regression tests also pass.

Cases cover duplicate/late/reused/early/unknown/negative release, id boundaries,
shared windows, queue/object/byte/private limits, ACK fairness and backpressure,
fragmented and partial mixed ACKs, duplex ids, interrupted graceful drain and

## QoS-2 complete-exchange CPU/heap/timing workload (2026-11-02)

Runtime baseline remains `77036057cdc6ca6577cf2056b54b5e119cbd3f89`. No product

duplex echo exchanges on one healthy loopback connection. They support MQTT

pinned comparator or accepted release baseline.

Sender latency ends at observer-visible final ACK; duplex additionally requires
the retained echo and peer-observed final receiver ACK. Taking a message does
not finish the measurement. Phase wall/CPU additionally includes observation
release and physical client-request retirement; copied native ACK tails can
remain until recorded connection teardown. Sequence stamps, separate request/
echo id spaces, phase checksums, owned data/ACK results and terminal counters
prevent a fast result from skipping either handshake. The peer decodes requests,
re-encodes/copies echoes and ACKs; its costs and observer polling are included.

200000 after 4096 internal warmup operations; cold/hot instrumented counts 20000
with 0/4096 internal warmup. Instrumented and uninstrumented binaries select

repeats / one process warmup, relative MAD 3%, central range 6%, and 5% throughput/

against a pinned baseline. Process CPU uses GetProcessTimes on Windows and

MQTT wire is 4 frames/60 bytes for v5 sender and 8/120 for duplex (v4: 59/118),
excluding handshake and TCP/IP/kernel framing. Full scope/cost/cleanup commands
are in `extlibs/xmqtt/bench/README.md`.

original requested QoS and Request Problem Information restrictions are checked.

acknowledgement/counts with a null owned Ack. The message clone now rebases ACK
reason views as well as existing publish/property views.

peer's maximum publication QoS. Partial-frame ordering, timeout/cancel after

## Bounded MQTT5 incoming Topic Alias (2026-11-02)

Baseline `665e191476b3e98731505c8aa5a982610cc7f3a4`. Positive MQTT5 CONNECT

entries before installing the replacement and refunding the old one. Messages

budgets. Their logical descriptor has the resolved topic; Wire retains the
actual empty-topic packet. Old messages survive remapping and all connection/

mapping. Dense-table footprint is explicit (maximum 65535 pointer slots), not

## Bounded MQTT5 outgoing alias snapshots (2026-11-02)

Baseline `165e202e57175ddff1f5d17ab76371b318277f71`. MQTT5 publishing now supports
full-topic alias bindings and explicit empty references. Successful admission
fixes each operation's logical topic, with a separately referenced latest-admitted
intent. The worker compares it with actual TCP packet order before first output,
compacting only a matching mapping. If an earlier unsent bind was cancelled,
timed out, rejected locally or blocked by Receive Maximum, a later reference
can safely carry its captured full topic. Delayed older publications also
recheck the actual mapping; they cannot retarget newer snapshots or overwrite
latest-admitted intent. No earlier publication is replayed. Peer alias limits
and actual selected local/peer packet caps apply before sending. Unknown empty
references and invalid aliases fail admission without changing the Future or
cache intent. Failed/overloaded/closed admission cannot install a new intent.

The existing 104-byte Request is unchanged. Aliased operations add one aligned
48-byte tail plus 0..7 bytes of padding in their existing allocation, charged
to private bytes through physical retirement. A lazy x64 2048-byte root and
4096-byte pages provide direct slots up to id65535; immutable topics have a
16-byte header plus their bytes. Planned, actual and request references use the
existing Gate. Common same-topic/empty references reuse cached storage. Ordinary
requests keep their original raw send loop without the gather stack/iteration.
Actual changed mappings are installed after the complete PUBLISH is accepted
into TCP; this is ordered stream state, not broker receipt or durable delivery.

Raw matching full binds and explicit compact references use one original buffer.
Compacting a full input gathers an inline prefix plus the copied original tail;
repairing an empty reference gathers prefix, captured topic and tail through
existing atomic XRT SendRefs. No Core API/shared runtime or second payload copy
is added. Each nonempty native span owns a real Request reference; NativeRefs,
physical id reservation and logical-topic lifetime include all release tails.
Partial frame ordering and QoS1/2 ACK decisions use actual selected wire length.
AcceptedBytes can therefore exceed or fall below retained descriptor encoding;
OutgoingBytes still counts the bounded retained snapshot, while optional metadata
and caches use MaxPrivateBytes and native bytes use Stream.WriteLimit.

Admission rollback now also handles late private-cache overload after constructing
the Promise/Future/result, and rechecks metadata room after cold identifier-table
allocation. It refunds every physical reservation and producer reference while
retaining only documented cold cache storage. OOM matrix and independent normal
private-cap overload cases cover rollback, unchanged output and destruction.
Queued cancel/zero timeout tests gate the protocol owner deterministically, and
check later snapshot topics and compact/full choices with one-byte write work.

The independent byte peer has 30 cases: normal and explicit compaction, mutable
intent snapshots, remaps, cancelled/timed-out binds, blocked QoS1 reorder plus
post-flow latest intent, actual peer rejection/local restriction, QoS1/2, ids and
topics through65535, Remaining Length width transitions, local/peer compact frame
caps, partial cancel/deadline/EOF, invalid/unknown aliases, private-cap overload,
directional duplex and graceful drain. Every observed publication's byte length
is compared independently with its Future's AcceptedBytes. Maximum topic data
is saved as size/hash. The new offline send example checks 23/14-byte QoS1 results
and cleanup after Client/Engine destruction.

## Explicit Cron timezone rule core (2026-11-02)

Added a developing `xcron_timezone` leaf, selected by the developing root, using
only public XRT time/memory/error/atomic APIs. It independently compiles explicit
POSIX TZ strings and RFC9636 TZif3 extended footer rules. There is no embedded
reference implementation, installed database, host TZ lookup or libc global
timezone dependency. Binary TZif loading, historical IANA transitions and zoned
calendar search remain pending; this is their required recurrence-rule engine.

The retained immutable owner makes one allocation for metadata, copied names
and (for DST) 800 cached int32 transition offsets over the 400 Gregorian years
2000..2399. Names are bounded at255 bytes and input at4096. It supports Jn/n/M
rules, default/explicit wall times, signed extended times, southern/negative/
zero-delta DST and perpetual/empty seasons. Missing DST rules return a typed
error instead of consulting ambient defaults. Queries expose exact state and
next effective change, full signed-int64 XRT civil decomposition, and all sorted
UTC candidates for a label. Gap=zero, fold=two; capacity discovery leaves the
candidate buffer intact. ERROR preserves candidate/Count outputs. Normal
queries/NONE/CAPACITY preserve ambient errors and allocate nothing.

XRT timestamps retain their 0001-01-01 epoch. The Unix oracle bridge explicitly
uses `XRT_TIME_UNIX_EPOCH`; exact epoch fixtures and core fixed-offset agreement
prevent a self-consistent roundtrip from masking a scale/calendar mistake.
Offset conversion avoids whole-timestamp overflow at either int64 endpoint.
Next search checks coalesced actual state changes and a complete403-rule-year
bound; a leap-only fixture crosses2096->2104 over the non-leap2100 century.

## Owned Cron TZif histories (2026-11-02)

Added independent `xcronZoneCreateTzif` for RFC9636 application/tzif v1..4 bytes.
It performs no file/name lookup, host TZ access or upstream implementation
embedding. Newer files skip the legacy block except for locating the authoritative
64-bit block. Main counts/bounds, strictly ordered transition seconds, references,
flags, offsets, name termination and footer consistency are validated. Native
history accepts all legal int32 offsets and full int64 transition seconds,
including values outside the XRT millisecond timeline. Out-of-timeline footer
consistency uses a corresponding Gregorian cycle. Empty/suffix-shared names work;
nonportable bytes produce an offset-derived numeric designation.

Creation prefilters redundant state changes, builds native binary-search tables,
descending unique offsets and unknown intervals, and owns copied names. It uses
one history allocation plus an optional retained POSIX footer allocation. Native
history lookup avoids civil decomposition; next-change lookup has no scan over
redundant raw records. Resolution checks at most258 offsets and supports arbitrary
multi-fold histories (a three-candidate independent fixture is included), with
sorted complete candidates and unchanged buffers on capacity/error outcomes.
Both parent and separately owned footer/unknown name aliases are protected.

RFC coverage is explicit: type0 before the first record, footer on/after the last,
unknown thereafter if it is absent, and type0 everywhere when there are no records
or footer. The -00 designation also means unknown. At/Split fail atomically with
typed UNKNOWN; NextTransition exposes coverage boundaries with the reserved
impossible offset sentinel. Resolution rejects incomplete candidates when an
unknown interval could map to the label under any legal int32 offset, instead of
publishing a guessed gap. This intentionally includes some known local labels
near truncated intervals. Leap-aware data receives structural/table checks and
typed SCALE rejection; leap conversion/truncation/expiration handling remains
pending. This stage does not claim application/tzif-leap completeness.

The direct selected public header now maps its required XRT features, verified
without including another extension header first. Public x64 state24/transition56/
issue24 stay unchanged on Windows and WSL. Private owner32->40 adds one pointer;
direct POSIX queries add a history-pointer branch. Further costs include cold
parsing/decode/name copies and table allocation, unique-offset work and binary
searches, and footer cycle reduction/public-call checks. The dedicated unpinned
4096-effective-change lookup smoke and updated isolated size reports run on both
systems. Other query paths, cold cost/CPU/allocations, contention, latency and
scheduler/reference performance still need profiling. No acceptance claim follows
from these short smoke samples; all measurement quality gates remain unchanged.

## Ordered actual Cron occurrences in zones (2026-11-02)

Added the developing `xcron_zoned` leaf with `xcronZonedMatch` and `xcronZonedNext`.

fixed offset, searches calendar masks and maps a result back with overflow-safe
arithmetic. It does not assume local labels increase across rollback, or assume

the next transition/end date. Whole-second granularity applies locally too:

second-level offsets and the full int64 XRT domain are supported.

## Bounded explicit-clock Cron scheduling kernel (2026-11-02)

Added the developing `xcron_scheduler` leaf with eleven public operations for
creation, admission, pull dispatch, completion, cancellation, job inspection,
retirement receipts, close, wake projection, statistics and destruction. One
preallocation bounds job/run slots, the due heap and intrusive queues within an
explicit byte cap. Expressions are copied; zones are success-only retained; Data
is borrowed through the retirement receipt. IDs use only the necessary low index
bits and all remaining generation bits, with nonwrapping terminal retirement.
A one-slot table uses all64 generation bits;128 slots retain57 bits. IDs are
scoped to one live scheduler, not global capabilities.

The owner supplies paired wall/monotonic millisecond samples. Monotonic rollback
fails atomically; wall rollback delays future work without rewinding consumed
cursors. Forward gaps use explicit catch-up/skip/coalesced misfires with a
saturating grace cutoff. Wait/allow/skip overlap and global/per-job running caps
include published leases and executor queue time. Alternating due promotion and
FIFO ready dispatch prevent an old catch-up job monopolizing the heap. Each Poll
has explicit work/output budgets. WorkLimit bounds actions, not CPU time inside
one recurrence search, which can still traverse full history/a Gregorian cycle.
The live adapter therefore still needs bounded/precomputed calculation work.

Completion is exactly once and acknowledges the physical body and data-using
tails. Success/failure/cancellation outcomes are counted without implicitly
stopping future triggers. Cancel/Close stop future dispatch while retaining live
leases. Only a terminal job with zero leases can return its Data receipt and
release its zone. Busy destruction preserves the owner. There are no callbacks,
threads, timers, executors or storage inside the kernel. Public XRT APIs suffice;
no Core/runtime change was introduced. A product-private pure zoned value query
records post-admission typed job faults without allocating/replacing ambient
errors. Public zoned validation, results and typed failure semantics remain.

## Actual XRT executor adapter for Cron leases (2026-11-02)

Added the developing `xcron_executor` leaf with nine public operations/types for
actual worker execution, cancellation, per-job cancellation, owned completion
receipts, close/inspection/destruction and a scoped cancellation query. It borrows
an existing public XRT Executor and creates no runtime, worker, timer or executor.
The creating native thread owns control/drain operations. A preallocated slot
array, <=50%-loaded lease-ID hash with backward-shift deletion and MPSC completion
publication bound all local storage within BytesLimit. Active IDs are scoped to
one originating scheduler. Successful admission transfers only the completion
return duty; rejection invokes no body and leaves the lease with its caller.

Callbacks borrow the copied64-byte Run/token and must finish data-using tails.
FAILED transfers that worker's ambient error into an owned receipt; invalid return
enums normalize to FAILED/RESULT without stealing another task's error. Queued
cancellation skips the body; running cancellation is cooperative and never
rewrites an already produced outcome. Close does not close a borrowed shared
executor. Drain copies an80-byte receipt and returns adapter capacity; the owner
then completes the kernel lease and eventually reaps Data. This is not an
exactly-once business-effect guarantee or a global lease capability.

The completion producer never accesses its slot/Data/Error after publication,
so a drained slot can be reused before its previous notification ends. A separate
producer reference protects adapter/notification context through that tail;
Destroy remains BUSY until receipts and producers are zero. Owner-notification
reentry and cross-thread control calls fail explicitly. Selecting a user body on
its adapter's owner thread returns typed OWNER_CONFLICT instead of entering owner
state. Optional Notify can signal a host event/post a wake; bounded resampling
must recover from failed wake delivery. No blocking adapter wait or new shared
runtime/Core API is introduced. Native thread-ID checks, hashing, copies, CAS
contention and public Executor bookkeeping remain explicit measured costs.

bounded attempts and explicit rejection/expiry/cancellation results. Native owner
and unrelated borrowed-pool callbacks cannot block waiting on the service.

TIMEOUT. Stable-owner query and final caller-entry exclusion remain required.

## 2026-11-12 - Bounded Cluster metadata seed evolution

Each published async-client map now refreshes the metadata seed plan using
eligible distinct masters, actual query origin and original bootstrap fallback.
A preallocated hash/index plan and copied host arena avoid allocation and
partial publication. Every later cache lookup still authorizes the exact
address. SHARDS selects explicit TCP/TLS ports, SLOTS preserves query transport,
SOURCE uses the copied query host, and unknown/unhealthy/replica/unavailable
endpoints are excluded. Bounds: <=MaxSeeds masters, <=2*MaxSeeds+1 total.
This genuinely adds constructor storage (default host arena17KiB) and metadata
CPU/copy work; warm-loop measurements exclude those cold costs.
Failed cohorts advance the next start candidate. Actual provider seed tracking
also preserves origin/progress when MaxWaits=0; accepted native query origin
remains separate. No native/Core/new shared runtime/public struct changes.

Tests cover SHARDS/SLOTS discovery, exhausted-budget zero-allocation selection,
original seed failure, non-bootstrap query-origin fallback, bootstrap fallback,
active-cohort rejection, immutable retained maps/results, small attempt limits,
zero-wait/full-cache cursor progression, TLS/SOURCE/unknown/replica fixtures,
constructor/cohort/call OOM, original deadlines and physical retirement.
Development constructor-budget and cold-readiness assertion corrections are
recorded with failed logs. No policy or protocol fallback was relaxed.

## 2026-11-12 - Immutable command key specifications

New xredis_command_keys parses COMMAND/COMMAND INFO into one retained immutable
Reply plus one bounded command/specification/hash allocation. Modern/legacy
rows, nested/partial subcommands, actual RESP3 Set collections, index/forward/
reverse keyword search, relative/negative/factored ranges and key-count rules
are supported. Unknown/incomplete/future rules remain typed server-assistance
requirements; they are never guessed as keyless. All routing keys, including
not_key, participate in binary CRC/hash-tag and cross-slot validation. Access
flags are possible metadata and do not authorize replica reads. No I/O or new
shared runtime. Automatic metadata fetch/fallback/Cluster submission is pending.

Constructor caps include retained Reply and hash work. Warm reads allocate no
storage or references, but validate descriptors and scan/hash arguments/keys.
An optional caller vector adds a second extraction pass without repeated CRC.
Search/key-occurrence/key-byte caps include hash collisions and overlapping
specifications. Failure never publishes partial key/output arrays.

Tests cover192 independent command-grammar models, literal modern/legacy/
nested/unknown/variable/binary cases, malformed late rows/duplicates, capacity/
aliases/wrapped spans, exact retained-byte caps, OOM prefixes,80 colliding names,

12000-cycle retained readers and single-only refcount overflow rollback.

## 2026-11-12 - Metadata-checked Cluster command submission

New optional xredis_cluster_command routes an immutable catalogue invocation
through the existing async client. Full-key CRC/slot checks precede admission;
unknown/incomplete/cross-slot/arity/work/byte refusals are typed and publish no
Future or business. Keyless commands require an explicit fallback, with NO_SLOT
returning KEYLESS. Empty binary keys remain slot0 routing keys. Preflight refusal
leaves client admission counters unchanged; native capacity/close/error counts
and existing result/redirect/cancel/physical shutdown contracts are preserved.

Function-entry time precedes metadata CPU and is forwarded into the shared
admission path, original route deadline and native Entered/Timeout. No catalogue
ref or extra copy/allocation/worker/timer/runtime is added. Warm caller budgets
compare actual blocks/bytes against explicit Call and retain the four-block
bound. Cold queued copies and native independent physical duties remain.

Tests cover caller-poisoned warm/cold input, catalogue budget retirement while
Future is pending, explicit keyless/default/zero timeout, empty slot0 key,
unknown/incomplete/cross-slot, overlapping key-byte and keyword-work limits,
client argument limits, catalogue/Reply/map/input aliases, native overload, OOM
prefixes, MOVED/ASK, timeout/cancel/close, retained results and four producers.
Single-only caller clock and native-owner probes check exact entry/deadline
equality, including the configured default. Prototype runs passed before freeze.

## 2026-11-12 - Synchronous native Cluster facades

Optional explicit-slot and metadata-routed synchronous APIs reuse the original
async operation/Future/native pools. All workers of both active dependent
Engines are refused before admission. The original function-entry timestamp
precedes worker/output checks and metadata, and reaches native deadlines.
Admission, actual native wait and typed Redis outcomes remain separate.
Only ACCEPTED publishes the complete {Wait,Future}; even wait failure transfers
the accepted possibly-pending Future for later wait/cancel/cleanup. No second
relative timeout, runtime object, worker, timer, queue, copy or result allocation.

Tests cover cold/default/zero calls, both Engines/all their workers and unrelated
worker success, overload/closed metadata after Engine teardown, full-span aliases,
no-allocation typed preflight refusals, actual MOVED/ASK, held native timeout/Close,
OOM prefixes and four concurrent callers. Held-worker budgets compare actual
async+Wait/sync blocks and bytes and retain the four-allocation bound. Selected
single caller-clock/native-owner probes verify exact original/default deadlines;
caller-only native-wait injection proves pending Future transfer and continued
progress. This is not a claimed real OS wait failure. Initial test-owner const
compilation failure was corrected before freeze; its failed log is retained.

Mainline verification: Windows 52 / WSL 54 programs.
Focused/single WSL ASan/UBSan/leak and two TSan units, full root and feature-off
client/command suites, root/leaf single/static/shared, isolated declarations,
both new exports/private hiding, API/docs/maturity and both minimal footprint
profiles pass. Explicit-slot minimal builds contain no command catalogue/routing
symbols. Feature-excluded client/node-cache old/current .text matches exactly.
Core/native client/pool and existing public layouts remain unchanged.

Real Redis8.0.5:288 cases/9216 INCR over4 forms/two hosts retain actual owned
node identities/epochs, three-view convergence, SHARDS/SLOTS, three factories/
init modes, real owner-change MOVED/migration ASK, discovered seed policy
recovery and physical Drop/outcomes. Four producers alternate both synchronous
APIs, check actual wait outcomes and prove exactly32 unique INCR effects/case.
Plaintext owned WSL servers do not qualify real TLS/replicas/process-death/native
Linux or production. Local stop still leaves native physical duties to Nodes.

## 2026-11-12 - Bounded RPC stream framing

New independent xrpc_frame supports strict Content-Length/ASCII/CRLF/UTF-8 media
headers and an explicit uint32-be profile. The serialized reader publishes only
complete opaque bodies, preserves coalesced suffixes and makes EOF/truncation/
protocol/unsupported/quota/OOM failures explicit and sticky. Complete current
bodies borrow caller bytes; fragments copy into reusable bounded storage.
Whole headers parse caller bytes, fragmented headers append/scan once then parse
once. Prefix/full writers preflight all spans before writing. No JSON, Future,
network, lock, thread, callback or new shared runtime. A production process/
stdio adapter, bidirectional runtime, WebSocket and negotiation remain open.

Tests cover independent wire bytes and every split, coalesced/empty/binary frames,
header/media grammar, length-digit transitions through1GiB without body allocation,
body/head/line/field/old+new reservation caps, reserve after borrowed/partial/failed
frames, poisoned copies, aliases/wrapped capacities, constructor and buffer OOM,
EOF/sticky failures,12000 mutations and10000 warmed zero-requested-heap cycles
per profile. Initial prototype include/warning/fixture-encoder errors and an
empty-first-header-line MORE bug were corrected before source freeze; logs kept.

Windows/WSL each pass 23/23 programs, including20 full root programs/host, focused and selected single.
WSL focused/single ASan/UBSan/leak pass. TSan is not applicable to this serialized
unique-owner pure reader (no concurrent mutable API contract). Leaf four forms,
isolated declarations, pure frame static/shared and encode-only static consumers,
root single/static/shared,11 exports/private hiding, API/docs/maturity and all
minimal footprint artifact symbol inventories pass. Core/old runtimes unchanged.

An existing consumer forced XRPC_MODULE_XRPC and broke partial package linking
on both hosts. It now honors feature selection, retaining root checks and an
independent encode-only path. Only that consumer changed after successful formal
unit/root/single/sanitizer tests. Both source maps and failed link logs remain;
exact source-equivalence records prove unchanged runtime, headers, tests, tools
and fixtures. New delivery/size/performance runs use the revised consumer map.

Real stdin/stdout:432 Python/C cases over4 build forms/two hosts, two profiles,
1/7/4096-byte reads, UTF-8 and NUL string ids, exact huge numeric ids, notifications,
empty/malformed JSON, mixed batches, coalescing, truncation, limits and hostile
headers. Child processes are terminal. This finite synchronous fixture is not
production pipe backpressure/cancel/close or bidirectional runtime acceptance.

## 2026-11-18: live receive commit and ACK ordering

The developing numeric TCP Client now persists each accepted PUBLISH before ACK
on MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1. QoS 2 duplicates reuse committed receive identities.
PUBREL and identifier retirement commit atomically before PUBCOMP. The delivery
remains in the durable store until explicit application acknowledgement. The
next connection can repeat the appropriate PUBCOMP for a lost response and
reuse the retired packet identifier. This follows the broker retry ordering in
[MQTT 5.0](https://docs.oasis-open.org/mqtt/mqtt/v5.0/os/mqtt-v5.0-os.html)
and [MQTT 3.1.1](https://docs.oasis-open.org/mqtt/mqtt/v3.1.1/mqtt-v3.1.1.html).

operations at the final sync. It verifies no premature ACK, late Close across
both acceptance and retirement, native file recovery, fresh Session import and
resumption, MQTT 5 alias canonicalization, storage refusal and full Inbox refusal.
One transaction per received message or known PUBREL is the current policy.
The private driver still needs durable leases, outgoing flows, and the full
transport and authentication integration. Controlled throughput and tail latency
and the native 72-hour acceptance remain outstanding.
See [stage evidence](xmqtt-client-store-receive-20261118.json).


## 2026-11-18 Durable application delivery leases

The Writer now offers an explicit lease mode for MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1. Its ready
queue grows only with committed deliveries and shares the existing MaxInbox
bound. Application buffers own the copied bytes. An opaque value fences stale
claims and earlier Writer instances without holding the file, pool or Writer alive.
An accepted ACK consumes the claim and publishes its actual durable effect. A
definite non-commit makes the record eligible for another claim. Recovery restores
unacknowledged deliveries in acceptance order.

The same Writer sequences application ACKs and live protocol transitions. The
fixture holds an application ACK at its final file sync and queues an incoming
PUBREL on the actual TCP Client. The application effect commits first. PUBCOMP
follows independent receive-identity retirement. Raw Inbox ACK deltas remain
available on the legacy Writer and cannot bypass leases in the explicit mode.

## 2026-11-18 Durable MQTT reconnect over TLS and WebSocket

The public example uses the same reconnect controller over numeric TCP, verified
TLS and native WS/WSS Client factories. The tracked Mosquitto driver drops the
first PUBACK, PUBREC or PUBCOMP and retires the original connection. It checks
Session Present, original identifiers, PUBLISH versus PUBREL retransmission,
subscriber payload/count and the durable END on the replacement.

The matrix runs both MQTT versions over TCP, TLS 1.2/1.3, WS and WSS 1.2/1.3.
Windows and WSL each exercise modular, single-header, static and shared forms.
The WSL modular matrix additionally runs with ASan, UBSan and leak detection.
Existing TCP cold recovery, uncertain-write and lease regressions remain
covered. Strict release still reports 32 developing modules. Broker-native
WS/WSS graceful shutdown, durable subscriptions and controlled production
throughput and tail latency remain open.

## 2026-11-18 Native file locking for MQTT journal owners

The locked constructors reject simultaneous owners of the same native file
during initialization, replay, append and physical teardown. The same lock
survives transfer to the typed Store Writer and continues to exclude contenders
after Close and Wait. Retaining the original Future value does not keep the
file locked after Writer Destroy.

Windows and Linux under WSL verify lock contention through independent opens,
hard-link aliases, constrained allocation, and fresh-process recovery after
normal close and forced process exit. Modular and single-header builds also
run the typed commit fixture. The static and shared consumer probes initialize,
reopen and append the same journal through their public headers.

The owner requires a pre-existing regular file in a trusted stable directory.
Directory durability, namespace replacement and compaction have separate
requirements.
[Stage evidence](xmqtt-locked-journal-20261118.json).

## 2026-11-18 Bounded journal generation switch

The native journal slot keeps its control lock through old-owner retirement
and selects one of two pre-provisioned data files. Replacement initialization
and appends sync before publication. The control map records the published
prefix. A worker can append after publication and the same handle remains
selected through physical destruction.

Windows and Linux under WSL test normal and abandoned preparation, allocation
refusal, generation exhaustion, typed Worker handoff and graceful removal.
An independent selector corpus tests interruption and torn pages using
native recovery. Injected selector write and flush failures verify the
uncertain result, poisoned write ownership, and fresh recovery. Static and
shared examples run creation, rotation and snapshot recovery. Preparation
and publication are explicit storage operations. MQTT snapshot encoding, automated compaction, initial namespace
power-loss qualification and controlled production performance remain open.
[Stage evidence](xmqtt-journal-slot-20261118.json).


## 2026-11-18 Offline MQTT store compaction

MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1 typed journals can be compacted under the native slot lock.
An independently reopened store preserves packet stages, ordered Inbox
deliveries, issued-key fences and expiry. A new semantic Writer consumes the
recovered State and its exact Journal, commits an old-epoch Inbox ACK, fences
a reused key, and appends a newer key. Repeating compaction preserves the
combined checkpoint and delta history.

Windows and Linux under WSL exercise modular and single-header reconstruction,
native faults, independent checkpoint bytes, and static/shared library examples.
The fixtures reduce a 15- or 16-transaction history to three transactions.
Live compaction scheduling, namespace and device power-loss qualification,
and production throughput and tail latency remain open.
[Stage evidence](xmqtt-store-compact-20261118.json).


## 2026-11-18 Online MQTT store rotation

The typed Writer can queue a checkpoint without retiring its Client.
Both MQTT versions complete durable QoS 1 round trips on the same TCP
connection across publication. The acknowledgement from an existing Inbox
lease becomes the first new-generation delta. Fresh
recovery verifies later delivery keys and END. Native fault tests exercise
cancellation during candidate I/O, continued use after inactive-write failure,
and fencing plus recovery after an uncertain selector publication.

The caller chooses the maintenance trigger. Other durable requests wait
behind the bounded checkpoint. Production throughput, tail latency, automatic
maintenance policy, and power-loss validation remain open.
[Stage evidence](xmqtt-store-compact-online-20261118.json).


## 2026-11-18 Online checkpoint recovery against Mosquitto

A real publisher rotates its typed MQTT store with an unfinished QoS 2
transaction, exits through native process termination, and resumes from
the synchronized slot in a fresh process. The broker preserves its session.
The independent wire observer verifies the original identifier and the
correct PUBLISH or PUBREL replay. The subscriber receives one copy. Fresh
typed replay verifies the final durable END.

The matrix covers Windows and Linux under WSL, MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1, TCP,
TLS 1.2/1.3, WebSocket and WSS, plus modular, single-header, static and shared
consumers. Automatic maintenance scheduling, device power-loss qualification,
and production throughput and tail latency remain open.
[Stage evidence](xmqtt-compact-crash-20261118.json).


## 2026-11-18 Automatic MQTT store compaction

MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1 Store Writers now support automatic checkpointing on the
existing storage pump. The queued foreground work precedes an idle rotation.
When an otherwise valid Inbox ACK reaches the physical file cap, the pump
can rotate and commit the same acknowledgement once on the new generation.
The fallback preserves the original deadline and lease reservation.

Native tests check growth-based suppression, a time-based retry without new
commits, manual reset of retry gates, explicit Close during candidate I/O,
and selector uncertainty. Windows and WSL run these checks through normal
and single-header builds. Static and shared consumers exercise the policy
through the public example. A 128-transaction pressure fixture rotates 21
times per platform and cold-reopens the last key on generation 22.
Production throughput and tail latency,
typed replay-quota scheduling, independent broker coverage for the new
automatic policy, and device power-loss qualification remain open.
[Stage evidence](xmqtt-store-compact-auto-20261118.json).


## 2026-11-18 Mosquitto verification of automatic MQTT checkpoints

Both automatic maintenance paths preserve a pending QoS 2 publish and a
broker-acknowledged Inbox delivery through native process termination.
The idle path stores both entries in the checkpoint. The physical-cap path
writes the inbound acceptance once on the newly selected journal. Independent
byte checks enforce the boundary and recovery completes the protocol exchange
and the separate application ACK.

Windows and Linux under WSL run the native clients through TCP, TLS 1.2/1.3,
WebSocket and WSS. Mosquitto stays alive during each replacement. The native
Linux production soak, storage-device power-loss and production throughput
and tail latency remain open.
[Stage evidence](xmqtt-store-auto-broker-20261118.json).

## 2026-11-18 Foreground MQTT replay capacity

A valid foreground transaction can now trigger online compaction under the
optional native Writer policy when the transaction, operation or replay-byte
budget is exhausted. The Writer proves the checkpoint and the pending
transaction fit together before writing. It suppresses repeated measurements
for an oversized batch at the same cut and lets a smaller batch trigger
maintenance. Inbox ACKs retain their original lease and deadline and commit
once after a successful rotation.

Windows and Linux under WSL cover MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1, plus simultaneous file
and replay pressure, invalid semantic batches, inability to fit, unchanged-cap
cold recovery, and uncertain selector publication. The rollback and retry
cases run through modular and single-header builds. Broker-connected replay
pressure, native Linux production runs, storage-device power-loss and
queue-inclusive throughput and tail latency remain open.
[Stage evidence](xmqtt-store-replay-quota-20261118.json).

## 2026-11-18 Mosquitto verification at MQTT replay limits

The independent broker runner exhausts transaction count, operation count
or replay bytes while retaining physical file headroom. Each old generation
is decoded and counted before the replacement starts. Each new generation
contains a QoS 2 checkpoint followed by one durable QoS 1 acceptance.
Restart uses the same replay cap and completes the QoS 2 exchange, the
recovered application Inbox ACK and graceful END. The wire observer verifies
that the original subscriber receives one copy.

The matrix covers native Windows and WSL clients, MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1,
TCP, TLS 1.2/1.3, WebSocket and WSS, and modular, single-header, static

## 2026-11-18 Fixed-arrival MQTT Store Writer capacity

Added a registered native-disk workload for MQTT 5.0 and 3.1.1. Latency
runs from the planned arrival through admission, queueing, checkpointing
and Future completion. Window drops, Writer admission refusal and accepted
timeouts reconcile with the exact scheduled count. A separate endpoint
includes physical drain. Every successful workload reopens the selected
journal and checks the final sequence and key fence.

Forty repeated local trials retain the existing noise-gate failures.

## 2026-11-18 Sentinel replica discovery

The standalone xredis Sentinel owner now offers explicit replica discovery.
It validates bounded RESP2 and RESP3 replica lists, skips down rows, and
hands out the first native Client with a connected replica ROLE response.
Failed candidates retire physically before the next candidate starts.
Per-candidate deadlines, fallback seeds, cancellation and the original total
deadline share the existing discovery state machine. One immutable seed reply
backs the candidate views through selection.

Redis failover tests exercise RESP2, RESP3 and AUTO with numeric, DNS and
prepared-address factories. Windows and WSL each verify the replica before
failover, the unknown-service outcome, and the demoted replica after failover,
with complementary master controls. The fixtures also exercise TLS, malformed
and over-budget lists, stale ROLE, timeouts and constructor OOM. Modular,
single-header and verified static/shared consumers cover the new entry point.

Replica pools, automatic seed refresh and event-triggered rediscovery remain
open. Native Linux long runs, real authenticated/TLS Sentinel deployments
and production throughput and tail latency remain qualification work.

## 2026-11-18 Sentinel replica pool failover

The xredis Sentinel pool now supports an explicit replica factory. The first
connection selects one connected, ROLE-verified replica. Refill can proceed
in parallel after selection. A repair tries the current endpoint first when
Sentinel still lists it. A different verified endpoint fences old leases,
preserves accepted command outcomes, and drains before serving the new
generation. The same pool recovers when an empty eligible list later gains a
replica.

Real Redis tests cover 18 replica pool failovers and 18 master pool controls
on Windows and WSL across RESP2, RESP3 and AUTO and three connection factories.
The C probe keeps three old leases and a queued acquisition alive across
promotion. It observes the accepted blocking command on the old server and
checks for no replay on the new endpoint. The final probe releases resolved
close observers during retries and bounds live observers at five.
A Windows master control attempt hit a Windows-reserved Sentinel port.
The failure and native bind error are retained beside the successful repeat.

Modular and single-header suites, static and shared package consumers,
ASan/UBSan/leaks, and TSan passed. Strict release still reports 31 developing
xredis modules. Automatic Sentinel seed refresh, event-triggered discovery,
real authenticated/TLS Sentinel deployments, native Linux endurance and
production throughput and tail latency remain open.
[Stage evidence](xredis-sentinel-replica-pool-20261118.json).

## 2026-11-18 Active Sentinel pool topology refresh

Master and replica pools can request an explicit refresh or opt into a
monotonic interval. Hints coalesce into one probe and at most one queued
follow-up. The probe queries Sentinel and verifies ROLE, preserving current
members on an unchanged endpoint or an optional probe failure. Verified
changes fence and physically retire the old generation before refilling.
Missing members preempt optional probes. The existing pool worker and timer
own every step and physical closure.

The real Redis fixture remaps Sentinel between two reachable masters. The
old server still reports master and holds a blocking client request when
the C probe sends the hint. Eighteen such remaps cover Windows and WSL,
three native connection factories, RESP2, RESP3 and AUTO. Thirty-six
independent master and replica election controls exercise default behavior.
Local fixtures also cover periodic refresh, reentrant Close, coalescing,
malformed replies, stale ROLE and cancellation for required refill. Modular,
single-header and package consumers, ASan/UBSan/leaks and TSan passed.

Additional Sentinel seed discovery and a packaged Sentinel Pub/Sub
listener remain open. The strict release gate still reports 31 developing
modules. Authenticated TLS deployments, native Linux endurance and
production throughput and tail latency remain qualification work.

## 2026-11-18 Sentinel seed learning and recovery

Master and replica pools can opt into endpoint-based seed factories and
learn additional Sentinel addresses. The pool copies configured seeds and
keeps a bounded exact-address table. One discovery at a time may query
SENTINEL SENTINELS. Each discovery sends that optional command at most
once, within the original seed and target budgets. A fully validated list
is appended only after ROLE verifies the data endpoint. Learned seed
errors can fall through to the configured addresses.

Windows and WSL each repair a pool after the configured Sentinel process
exits and its port refuses connections. Thirty-six real Redis cases cover
both data roles, three connection factories, and RESP2, RESP3 and AUTO.
Two original leases stay usable on the same data endpoint and generation.
Fifty-four real Redis controls cover existing election and online refresh
paths. Local fixtures also cover TLS, malformed/oversized/empty lists,
readiness faults, two stale ROLE attempts and constructor allocation
failure. The package example runs the learned endpoint path.

A packaged Sentinel Pub/Sub listener remains open. The strict release gate
still reports 31 developing modules. Authenticated TLS interoperability,

The optional xredis_sentinel_events leaf reuses the subscription session,

## 2026-11-18 Redis Sentinel mutual TLS and ACL elections

A disposable Redis 8.0.5 topology uses TLS-only listeners, mandatory client

The native probe pins TLS 1.2 or 1.3, verifies the server name and CA, and
rejects wrong passwords on both connection roles before preparing the pool.
The fixture also checks missing client identity, cleartext, missing Redis
authentication, cross-role credentials and restricted commands.

pools, both TLS versions, RESP2/RESP3/AUTO and numeric, DNS and prepared-address
factories. The listener observes the real switch event. A queued acquisition

The runner uses the WSL local filesystem for its temporary replication data
and TLS material. Initial mounted-filesystem synchronization failures and

Build the existing interop probe with SPR_TLS and the
xredis_sentinel_events, xredis_tls_auth, tls_identity_rsa and pem modules.
The runner accepts --listen master or --listen replica and --tls 12 or --tls 13.

## 2026-11-18 Sentinel lease recovery latency

The xredis_sentinel_event_recovery profile measures the time for a saturated
master or replica pool to replace its generation and serve queued acquisitions.
Both triggers keep a RESP3 subscription online. The direct control calls
xredisSentinelPoolRefresh. The Pub/Sub case schedules a +switch-master frame
on the loopback Sentinel peer. Timing starts just before dispatch and stops
when the caller observes the first queued lease and then the entire cohort.
Each transition checks the new endpoint and generation, physical retirement
of the old leases, and a binary ECHO on the verified replacement peer.
The pool uses WorkItems=1 and the default MaxConnecting=4, capped at capacity.

Each of the eight cases runs five measured processes of 1,024 transitions
per platform. A process discards its first eight transitions. The runner
uses one separate process warmup. Each transition begins at least 2 ms
after observation of the previous cohort. The rate is computed over active
recovery windows. The JSON reports retain p50, p95, p99 and p99.9 per repeat,
plus the maximum and the active recovery rate.

| Pool | Slots | Trigger | Windows first / all p99 (ms) | WSL first / all p99 (ms) |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| master | 1 | direct | 1.561 / 1.561 | 1.511 / 1.511 |
| master | 1 | pubsub | 1.673 / 1.673 | 1.560 / 1.560 |
| master | 8 | direct | 2.424 / 4.135 | 1.862 / 2.955 |
| master | 8 | pubsub | 2.285 / 3.934 | 1.985 / 3.108 |
| replica | 1 | direct | 1.534 / 1.534 | 1.554 / 1.554 |
| replica | 1 | pubsub | 1.685 / 1.685 | 1.639 / 1.639 |
| replica | 8 | direct | 2.187 / 3.812 | 1.951 / 3.095 |
| replica | 8 | pubsub | 2.160 / 3.715 | 1.952 / 3.036 |

The table reports medians of per-process p99 values. The ordinary
repeatability limits are 3% relative MAD and 6% relative central range.
Windows recorded 47 threshold breaches and WSL recorded 33.
These measurements remain exploratory because the limits were exceeded.
Host isolation was unverified, and a separate validation process was observed
while the WSL runner was in setup.
Modular regressions passed on Windows (5 programs) and WSL (5 programs).
All six repository checks passed. ASan, UBSan and leak detection also passed for both
8-slot Pub/Sub workloads in WSL.

Run from the main checkout with GCC available in PATH.

```text
python tools/measure_performance.py --config extlibs/xredis/config/performance_profiles.json --profiles xredis_sentinel_event_recovery --report out/xredis-sentinel-event-recovery.json
```

This workload isolates client-side replacement after a topology change.
Measuring real election lag, sustained business traffic during failover and
native Linux performance remains part of production qualification.
[Stage evidence](xredis-sentinel-recovery-bench-20261118.json).

## 2026-11-18 Fixed-arrival load during real Sentinel failover

The interop probe starts with three native exclusive pool members
and a Sentinel subscription. One producer offers binary 32-byte PING
requests at predetermined monotonic times. Each offer acquires a lease
and issues at most one command within the remaining budget. The ledger
includes capacity drops, acquisition and call results, deadline misses
and delivery states. It validates every returned payload. The probe
checks the original and replacement Redis process identities and
waits for physical closure.

The 18-second diagnostic uses 64 generator slots and a 200 ms budget.
The controller issues SENTINEL FAILOVER at a marker roughly one second
into the stream. A paired control uses the same stream without an
election. Latency is measured from the planned arrival. The measured
transition starts at the trigger marker and ends when the caller
observes the new endpoint, generation and full pool membership. The
controller separately records its command and role-observation times.
[Redis Sentinel documentation](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/oss_and_stack/management/sentinel/).

| windows | master | mTLS 1.3 | 1,000 | 17,999/18,000 | 47.990 | 1.262 |

scheduled offers across 10 real failovers and their controls.

generator dropped 1,078 offers before lease admission. The ledger

The initial Windows replica observation at
12 seconds ended before Redis had finished converting the old master

A three-node Redis fixture reproduced the replica pool adopting a standby

Replica discovery now excludes a row with the promoted flag and requires the
other candidates to report its exact endpoint as upstream in ROLE. Conflicting
promoted endpoints leave the snapshot retryable. A formerly preferred replica
that now reports primary invalidates a snapshot that missed the promotion.

retirement before trying another candidate.

standby before traffic begins. During failover the C probe publishes a marker
after full replacement and a verified binary PING offered on the replacement
generation. The controller then observes the standby following the promoted

## 2026-11-18 xcron pull scheduler job checkpoints

The optional xcron_checkpoint module saves a quiescent actual or selected
job in a 180-byte versioned record. It binds configuration and application
job/revision keys, carries counters and next occurrence, and rejects
incompatible or corrupt input before acquiring a slot or a zone reference.
Restoring an exhausted or explicitly cancelled job preserves its terminal
state. The monotonic epoch and process-local Data come from the new owner.
A selected restore revalidates the instant and reconstructs the local label
and multiplicity. The job record is separate from the dispatch path.

Windows and WSL modular and single-header tests cover CRC corruption, a
valid-CRC off-schedule cursor, configuration mismatch, active lease and
unfinished search rejection, cancelled/exhausted jobs, DST folds, and typed
errors under allocation refusal. The isolated module and full package
pass static and shared consumer tests. ASan, UBSan and leak detection
pass in WSL. The isolated size profile checks the file/thread/executor
dependency boundary.

The independent processes flush the last complete record, acquire a live
lease and terminate its process before completion. Restart reoffers that
lease. After committing a new record, a later restart advances to the next
instant. Windows and WSL produce byte-identical records and reject a
truncated input file. Run the test with the built checkpoint example as
the client. [Checkpoint example](../../extlibs/xcron/examples/checkpoint/README.md).

Five repeats of 150,000 operations use one precompiled UTC job and a
serialized owner. The restore rate includes cancellation and reaping
each restored job. These are in-memory operation rates.

| Platform | Save records/s | Restore and reap records/s |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| windows | 1,552,996 | 1,245,724 |
| wsl | 1,537,288 | 1,220,409 |

The local runs pass the repeatability limits on both platforms. Storage
commit/rotation, live service integration, power-loss validation, native
endurance and end-to-end throughput and tail latency remain open. The
strict xcron release gate lists 14 developing modules.
[Stage evidence](xcron-checkpoint-20261118.json).

## 2026-11-18 File-backed xcron checkpoint store

The optional leaf keeps one job and revision in two slots of an 8192-byte
file. A caller-serialized handle owns the native exclusive lock. Commit
checks the generation and record envelope, writes the other slot and
synchronizes the file before updating the cache. A failed write or flush
requires a reopen to establish the recovered generation. Create is
exclusive and opening a corrupt file never reinitializes it.

Windows NTFS and WSL ext4 pass blocked-contender and process termination
checks with an active lease, a persisted torn prefix and a complete slot
before flush. After a torn write the prior generation is readable. With
the full slot visible after process termination, reopening synchronizes
and publishes the new generation. The earlier tmpfs controls produced
identical wire images. The modular fault probe also injects I/O failure
returns in the actual store implementation and checks poisoned handles.
The module, standalone header, package consumers and WSL sanitizers pass.

Each timing sample contains one alternate-slot write and native flush.

## 2026-11-18 Checkpoint capture and restore on the live xcron owner

An optional module connects both live service modes to the versioned
scheduler checkpoint. Opt-in construction budgets the record storage in
the arena. Commands share the existing FIFO, tickets, work limits and close
semantics. Restore copies the record and retains the configuration zone on
queue acceptance. The owner captures a quiescent job or validates and
restores its saved occurrence. File reads and synchronous commits run on
the calling or separate storage thread.

The modular and single-header suites cover actual and selected delivery,
selected policy restoration, active lease rejection, output preservation,
wrong collectors and keys, timeout, ticket saturation, startup OOM and
close with an accepted restore. Existing service and checkpoint suites,
trimmed and full static/shared consumers, and WSL sanitizers pass.

On Windows NTFS and WSL ext4, terminating the process with an active lease
left generation 1 unchanged. A fresh process replayed occurrence 1000,
completed it and committed generation 2. The next restart reported
occurrence 2000 and one success. A contender could not open the locked
store while the interrupted process was running. The corresponding
checkpoint file images were byte-identical across the two platforms.

The local benchmark uses five repeats of 10,000 serial capture requests.
It measures admission through collection of the record for one quiescent
UTC job. The table shows the median of each reported run statistic.

## 2026-11-18 Per-job pause and paused checkpoint recovery

Pull and live schedulers now hold new leases for one job through an

existing duties. The held cursor leaves the heap and ready or overlap
queues after any search finishes. On resume, configured misfire and
overlap policies apply to its original position. Paused restore installs
the hold inside owner-side admission, before an overdue cursor can
dispatch. The hold is runtime state and preserves the existing wire format.

The Windows and WSL tests verify unrelated job progress, no idle spin,

## 2026-11-18 Atomic checkpoint groups

The group store persists a bounded, sorted set of v1 job checkpoints
in one generation of a locked two-slot file. It validates the entire
input, writes one contiguous alternate image, then flushes and publishes.
Read borrows the validated cached group. Group identity and capacity are
fixed on reopen. The example stages two jobs paused before advancing
and committing them together. Existing single-job files remain unchanged.

The outer checksum binds ordered per-record CRC fields. Hashing the
complete record bytes including their own CRCs would give a fixed
residue and miss substitutions. The multi-page unit fixture replaces
one record with an individually valid record from another generation
and verifies whole-group fallback. Both damaged slots are rejected.
The suites cover allocation refusal, stale or duplicate inputs, lock
contention, empty commits, and uncertain handles.

Windows NTFS and WSL ext4 both revert to generation 1 when the writer
is terminated after persisting only the new header and first record.
When the process terminates after the full write but before its flush,
reopen validates generation 2 and synchronizes it before publication.
Each fixture's bytes agree across platforms. Module and single-header
tests, prior checkpoint regressions, trimmed and full static/shared
consumers, and WSL ASan, UBSan and leak checks pass. The size profile
checks that trimming excludes executor, thread and network entry points.

## 2026-11-18 Whole-group live service startup

The checkpointed constructors can start from a complete committed record
array with independent expected keys and configurations. The owner
installs the entire group before the startup handshake publishes
all job IDs and the service. Scheduled jobs start paused. A late member
failure reports its index and unwinds prior admissions without invoking
the clock or business callback. Terminal records preserve their normal
retirement. File reads and commits stay with the caller.

The temporary ID array is charged to retained-byte admission and
InitializationBudget and released before publication. Both service modes

array aliasing, empty groups, limited startup bytes, targeted scratch

checks that all IDs are visible when the owner starts its loop.

runs each job once. A single commit records both successors in generation 2.

and single-header suites, prior single-job restart and ordinary service
regressions, trimmed and full static/shared packages, and WSL ASan, UBSan
and leak checks pass. Clang 21 ThreadSanitizer passes the modular suite.

## 2026-11-19 Capture and hold a whole group online

Pull and live schedulers can validate every quiescent member and capture
all records at one owner boundary. A successful capture holds dispatch
for the scheduled members. A rejection preserves the previous holds and
the entire output. The tests force a late busy member and confirm that
an earlier eligible member still dispatches.

A live capture borrows the target and record arrays until collection,
uses one command ticket, and charges one turn unit per member. Counts
are bounded by JobLimit and CommandWorkLimit. A command whose cost
exceeds the remaining turn budget waits at the queue head. The
serialized pull capture succeeds with an allocation denial budget.

## 2026-11-19 Write a whole checkpoint group on a storage executor

The optional writer takes one open group and borrows a host XRT executor.
It admits one commit through collection. Admission borrows immutable
records and uses one existing executor slot. The storage worker checks
the expected generation and writes and flushes the same alternate slot
as the direct group API. The serialized store selection can still build
without the executor. The worker publishes the native outcome and any
owned diagnostic through a generation-bound collection ticket.

Deterministic tests hold the worker queue full, cancel a queued commit,
cancel the executor during physical flush, and fail the flush after the
slot write. They verify exact borrow release, no admission allocation,
constructor rollback, stale tickets, typed errors and refusal to destroy
before collection. A running write reports its actual result even when
the host cancels its executor. After an uncertain result, the test closes
the writer and reopens the file to resolve the generation.

The live example hands its captured records to a storage executor and
queries the scheduler before joining storage. Windows NTFS and WSL ext4
recover identical images. The restart, interrupted group write, base
service regressions, trimmed and full static/shared consumers, and
modular and single-header tests pass on both platforms. WSL sanitizer
runs cover ASan, UBSan, leaks and Clang ThreadSanitizer.

## 2026-11-19 Commit a live checkpoint group in one request

The live owner reserves a whole group through lease quiescence, capture
and an asynchronous file commit. It keeps dispatch protected until the
writer reports its outcome. Prior pauses survive success, definite storage
errors and executor rejection. An uncertain store leaves scheduled members
paused for reconciliation. Shutdown drains an admitted
write and returns the physical outcome before destroying the service.

Capture, handoff and release run in bounded owner turns. The integrated
operation fits the existing checkpoint command slot and borrows scratch
records through collection. One writer notification wakes the owner.
While storage is pending, the owner observes an atomic readiness flag
without acquiring the writer lock.

Deterministic tests block the storage executor and let an unrelated
due job finish while the reserved group cannot dispatch or be cancelled.
They cover a wait from the storage executor, mismatched collectors and
scratch aliasing, queued cancellation, storage rejection, stale generation,
uncertain store, preserved prior pauses and close with an admitted write.

The runnable example advances and recovers both jobs through the integrated
request. Windows NTFS and WSL ext4 produce identical durable images and
pass the restart, interrupted writer, base service, modular, single-header
and static/shared consumer checks. WSL passes ASan, UBSan, leak detection
and Clang ThreadSanitizer.

## 2026-11-19 Run periodic group checkpoints on the live owner

One registration occupies one existing command slot through final
collection. The owner takes its cadence from the host monotonic timer.
It skips elapsed ticks in constant work and admits at most one capture
or write at a time. Ordinary commands get a turn between attempts.
Successful writes advance the expected generation. Capture timeouts
and temporary storage rejection retry on a subsequent tick. A stale
or uncertain store stops the schedule. Stop and Close drain accepted
writes and release the arrays and writer after final collection.

The pressure tests hold a native storage worker while the tick cadence
passes, saturate its queue and hold a job through its capture deadline.
They also cover repeated generations, borrowed scratch aliasing, stale
schedule tickets, stopping before the first tick, closing with a write
queued and refusing a wait from the storage executor. The packaged
consumers exercise arm, inspect, stop and final collection.

Windows and WSL pass modular, single-header, static/shared consumer,
ordinary service and checkpoint regressions. An independent process
advances two jobs, commits their group periodically, and opens both
slots through the existing writer and service readers. Single-commit
and interrupted-write recovery still pass. WSL passes ASan, UBSan, leak
detection and Clang ThreadSanitizer.

The periodic example reopens generation 3 on Windows and 3 on WSL.
Both files have the same SHA-256 digest.

## 2026-11-19 xredis Cluster replica selection

`xredisClusterClientCallReplica` selects a usable replica from the slot's shard
under the original call deadline. The start position rotates across calls.
An immutable shard index bounds the scan to that shard. The source endpoint
inherits the topology query host and transport. Routes can fall back to an
eligible primary before native admission. After acceptance, validated MOVED
or ASK is the only routing retry.

Each replica profile uses its own authorized pool, even when its address also
has an ordinary pool. A factory candidate without managed READONLY cannot
enter the ready list. Failure and replacement use the native pool's physical
retirement path. The regular command APIs continue to select primaries.

Windows and Ubuntu/WSL pass modular and single-header Cluster and pool
regressions and independent static and shared consumers. The WSL managed
Cluster suite passes GCC ASan, UBSan and leak detection. Scripted peers
exercise cold bootstrap, both topology formats, rotation, loading-replica
filtering, provider denial, profile mismatch and recovery, MOVED and a
cancelled accepted read. Redis 8.0.5 tests actual binary reads for all four
RESP2/RESP3 and SHARDS/SLOTS combinations with both native clients. An initial
fixture run queried metadata before the owning primary advertised the
replica. The qualified fixture waits for both views.
